mission_07: Causal forests extend random forests to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects — how the causal effect of a treatment varies across individuals based on their characteristics. Unlike standard forests that predict outcomes, causal forests predict treatment effects τ(x) = E[Y(1) - Y(0) | X=x]. The key innovation is the causal splitting criterion: instead of minimizing prediction error, splits are chosen to maximize the difference in treatment effects between child nodes. Honest estimation, introduced by Athey and Imbens (2016), uses separate subsamples for determining tree structure and estimating leaf values, which ensures valid confidence intervals. You will implement a simplified causal forest with honest splitting, CATE estimation, and variable importance measures that identify which features drive treatment effect heterogeneity.
